book_use: Current Kalshi principle that contract rules define outcome criteria, information sources, and verification sources rather than relying on informal impressions of what happened; Chapter: 9; Notes: Used alongside Polymarket mechanics to show that rule-defined resolution is general to event contracts rather than unique to one platform.

title: Tech stocks lead Wall Street after Nvidia, Salesforce and others say AI is creating big growth
book_use: NVIDIA shares rose 8.7% on August 27 after its earnings and outlook, while the Nasdaq rose 1.6%; used to show a narrative and new financial information becoming an immediate market price; Chapter: 10; Notes: Secondary source used for same-day market reaction rather than corporate fundamentals; intraday narratives are not assumed to explain every component of the price move.

author_or_institution: Jared Kaplan; Sam McCandlish; Tom Henighan; Tom B. Brown; Benjamin Chess; Rewon Child; Scott Gray; Alec Radford; Jeffrey Wu; Dario Amodei
title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
book_use: Empirical power-law relationships between language-model loss and model size, dataset size, and training compute across wide ranges; establishes the narrow technical claim from which the chapter traces later narrative expansion; Chapter: 10; Notes: The paper concerns model loss and compute allocation, not corporate profit, economy-wide productivity, or the return on AI infrastructure.

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
book_use: Chinchilla result showing that compute-optimal performance depends on balancing model size and training data; a 70B model using more data outperformed much larger models at the same compute budget; Chapter: 10; Notes: Used as counterevidence to a simplistic bigger-is-always-better narrative and as an example of scientific scaling claims being refined rather than discarded.

title: GPT-4 Technical Report
book_use: OpenAI reported predicting GPT-4 final loss from runs using at most 1/10,000 of its compute and HumanEval performance from models using at most 1/1,000, while noting that some capabilities remained difficult to predict; Chapter: 10; Notes: Supports the engineering-stage transition from retrospective scaling laws toward pre-training capability prediction; chapter preserves the report's limitations.

title: Three Observations
book_use: Broader economic narrative linking AI resources to model intelligence, rapid declines in cost of a given intelligence level, expanding use, and an argument for continued exponential investment; Chapter: 10; Notes: Executive interpretation rather than peer-reviewed empirical work; the post states its forward implications conditionally and is used to show how a technical narrative broadens.

title: Narrative Economics
book_use: Framework for understanding economically consequential narratives as stories that spread and help motivate actions including spending and investing; Chapter: 10; Notes: Used as a conceptual lens; the chapter does not treat narrative as synonymous with falsehood or claim it uniquely explains AI asset prices.

author_or_institution: Sushil Bikhchandani; David Hirshleifer; Ivo Welch
title: A Theory of Fads, Fashion, Custom, and Cultural Change as Informational Cascades
book_use: Formal model showing why observing others' actions can rationally convey information while also producing conformity and potentially fragile cascades; Chapter: 10; Notes: Used to distinguish rational social learning from caricatures of herd behavior; the model is an analogy for information transmission, not a direct empirical estimate of AI investing.

title: Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for quarter ended June 30, 2026
book_use: Financing-risk evidence: more than $25B of debt, several delayed-draw term facilities with effective rates around 9%-15%, and $16.3B of operating lease liabilities; Chapter: 11; Notes: High-cost financing is treated as reduced tolerance for forecasting error, not proof that underlying capacity lacks demand.

title: CoreWeave Reports Strong First Quarter 2026 Results
book_use: Revenue of about $2.1B and revenue backlog of $99.4B at March 31, 2026, showing exceptional contracted demand alongside capital intensity and leverage; Chapter: 11; Notes: Backlog is subject to delivery and availability conditions and is not current-period revenue; used as counterweight to a financing-only bearish interpretation.

title: GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition
book_use: Pricing diagnostic: July 30 update cut GPT-5.6 Luna API pricing by 80% and Terra by 20%, while an August 21 update cut promotional Sol pricing by over 20% for three months; Chapter: 11; Notes: Observed list-price changes illustrate price compression and possible demand elasticity; vendor efficiency claims are not treated as independent market-wide measurements.

title: Railroad earnings improvement in first half of 1898
book_use: Reported roughly $61M year-over-year gross-earnings improvement across 232 roads and estimated about $70M improvement across the U.S. railroad system; Chapter: 12; Notes: Used to show operating recovery after the receivership wave without implying that old securities were restored.

author_or_institution: Global Crossing Limited / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
title: Global Crossing Form 10-K following Chapter 11 reorganization
book_use: Global Crossing's December 9, 2003 reorganization transferred substantially all old-company assets to New GCL, illustrating infrastructure survival through a change in capital structure; Chapter: 12; Notes: Used as the opening concrete case; the network's continued existence does not establish that every fiber asset retained full economic value.

title: ITU estimates two billion people online by end 2010
book_use: Global internet users exceeded two billion by 2010 and internet penetration reached about 30%, showing continued diffusion after the dot-com and telecom busts; Chapter: 12; Notes: Official international statistics; used as post-bust adoption evidence rather than a claim about investor returns.

title: About a Third of Workers Who Used AI in the Last Week Said They Completed Tasks One to Two Hours Faster
book_use: March 2026 household survey found 55% of U.S. workers had used AI on the job for at least one listed task; among recent users, many reported time savings; Chapter: 12; Notes: Self-reported survey evidence; task use and perceived time savings are not the same as measured firm-level productivity or investment returns.
